Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet. Attached is the Steward private deployment appendix with a prioritized list of constraints for on-prem and VPC models. Our security council wants a short written response to a few critical items before we onboard a vendor into our procurement queue:

1) Operator access model for air-gapped sites (we prefer minimal outbound egress and ephemeral operator sessions)
2) Patch/upgrade delivery for isolated environments (signed bundles only)
3) Integration points for customer HSMs for key material
4) Telemetry/telemetry-exfil restrictions and retention windows

Can your team provide a capability questionnaire and indicate the earliest available window for a 30-minute technical deep-dive this week? I attached the appendix.

Dana —

Thanks for sending the appendix and the prioritized list. We can absolutely respond in writing and walk through the items in a technical call. High level answers up front so your security council has context before the call: 

- Operator access: Redwood supports operator access via an operator bastion when customers permit outbound egress; for true air-gapped installs we support on-site operator sessions initiated by customer-run consoles and require HSM-based signing for any operator workflow that modifies runtime images or model artifacts.
- Patching/upgrades: We deliver signed patch bundles and provide a verification tool that runs locally to validate signatures and hashes before install.
- HSM integration: We support customer-managed network-attached HSMs (PKCS#11) and integrate with cloud HSMs for VPC options; keys for model encryption and signing can be kept customer-side.
- Telemetry: Telemetry collection is configurable — you can choose metrics-only (no traces/token content) with local retention; we support disabling all outbound telemetry for air-gapped deployments and an on-prem telemetry archive option.

I'll circulate a more detailed questionnaire and checklist. Vanessa, can you attach the hardening checklist and the latest network diagram variant we use for air-gapped installs?

Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Dana / Steering team —

Attaching the operational hardening checklist and a concise network diagram. Below are explicit answers and operational notes to the four items you highlighted: 

- Operator access model (air-gapped):
  * Default: no vendor-initiated outbound access. Operators must be physically onsite or use customer-provided jump-hosts.
  * Ephemeral sessions: operators authenticate using short-lived certs provisioned via customer PKI; session recordings are stored on-prem unless customer requests deletion.
  * Emergency break-glass: requires customer approval and is performed via signed, auditable change bundles.

- Patch / upgrade delivery:
  * We publish signed bundles (Ed25519 signatures) and provide a bundle verification binary that runs locally.
  * Upgrade paths are documented; rollback artifacts are included.
  * Customers can opt for a vendor-assisted model where the signed bundle and a deployment manifest are delivered on removable media (USB/air-gap transfer) or through an approved courier.

- HSM / Key material:
  * PKCS#11 and KMIP are supported; keys never leave the customer boundary when configured with a local HSM.
  * We can integrate with customer HSMs for code-signing keys for patches and for runtime encryption of caches.

- Telemetry & retention:
  * Configurable: metrics-only, metrics+alerts (no PII), full telemetry.
  * For air-gapped installs: telemetry collection can be disabled; if enabled, data is stored in customer-managed S3-compatible storage with retention configurable per deployment.

Suggested next steps: 1) Vendor questionnaire (I attached) — please mark fields that must be answered by your security team; 2) 30-min tech deep-dive (we have windows Wed 14:00–16:00 PT / Thu 09:00–11:00 PT); 3) If you want, we can provide a short runbook sample for operator emergency procedures.

Attachments: PrivateDeploy_HardeningChecklist.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), NetworkDiagram_v2.png (PNG)

—Vanessa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — good detail. A few follow-ups from our security team: 

1) Signed bundles only is a hard requirement. We need proof of your signing key rotation policy and evidence that boot/upgrade paths validate signatures end-to-end.
2) On HSMs: we require support for our on-prem HSM appliance (SafeBox v3) over PKCS#11 and a documented test plan we can run in our lab.
3) Telemetry: we will default to telemetry-disabled; if enabled later, retention must be explicit (90 days metrics; 0 retention for request payloads).
4) SOC 2 + pen test evidence: please provide the most recent SOC 2 report and a summary of recent penetration test remediation items.

Also — procurement needs an NDA before we can circulate sensitive architecture diagrams to the board. I'm uploading a short request doc. Can Redwood provide a draft NDA (DocuSign preferred) and the SOC2 artifact under NDA?

Oliver
Director, IT Security
Steward Health Systems
